D1 research authoring, batch 82 (2026-09-27): four ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1, 2, 3, and 4 (cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals, migraine-headaches, seizure-disorder, multiple-sclerosis) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. This is a DIRECTIONAL IDENTITY rather than a disease: the catalog scotoma is a visual field finding, not a condition with its own pathology, so every edge on this file is ETIOLOGIC and every causation status states the reverse arrow explicitly.

Classification and direction guard: all four edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) and all four causation statuses state in terms that the located evidence establishes that the TARGET produces the visual field defect, not that the scotoma produces the target. No edge on this file may be presented as a consequence relationship in the direction its name suggests. The four targets are registered as a COMPETING AETIOLOGICAL DIFFERENTIAL of a single presentation rather than as four independent routes: the located occipital-epilepsy cohort reports 75 percent co-morbid interictal migraine, and the located visual-aura systematic review states that migraine aura is often clinically difficult to distinguish from transient ischaemic attack and from epilepsy, so the three aetiologies are not cleanly separable in an individual. The rank 3 edge additionally discloses that its mechanism category NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION follows existing registry precedent for this target even though the located cohort describes a functional cortical discharge rather than a degenerative process, and that no category outside the controlled vocabulary was invented to resolve this.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no glaucoma and no cataracts edge (DUPLICATE-SCOPE and SCOPE - both are established causes of field loss and both identities carry incoming edges, but the located evidence assembled for this file concerns homonymous post-geniculate and optic-nerve defects rather than arcuate or glaucomatous field loss, so authoring them here would attach a different mechanism on the strength of no located anchor for this primary); no transient-ischaemic-attack-residuals edge (RECORDED AS AN UNRESOLVED GAP, since a transient ischaemic attack is the more common presentation of a transient scotomatous defect than occipital stroke, yet no located anchor assembled for this file addresses it, and the edge is therefore named as a gap in the rank 1 evidence-gaps field rather than authored without an anchor); no optic-neuritis edge (DUPLICATE-SCOPE and MISSING IDENTITY - the catalog identity is optic-neuritis and the registry already carries a multiple-sclerosis to optic-neuritis edge, so a scotoma to optic-neuritis route would insert an indirection between a finding and a cause it already reaches through the rank 4 edge); and no visual-impairment edge (TARGET-EXHAUSTION - visual-impairment carries seventeen registered incoming edges and is a functional consequence rather than an aetiology, so a scotoma to visual-impairment edge would restate a consequence the registry already resolves from the conditions that actually cause it).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Occipital infarction is the commonest documented cause of a homonymous visual field defect, and the located evidence both establishes that ranking and characterises the residual defect: a cohort of 36 patients with acute occipital stroke reports that stroke is the most common cause of homonymous visual field defects, that 26 of 36 patients (72 percent) had a visual field defect at onset identified by confrontation or perimetry, and that at follow-up more than one year later 13 patients (36 percent) had a remaining defect comprising 5 homonymous hemianopias, 5 homonymous quadrantanopias, and 3 homonymous scotomas, with macular ganglion cell and inner plexiform layer and retinal nerve fibre layer thickness significantly reduced in each eye in patients with a defect compared to those without (p<0.01 for all comparisons) (PMID 34487632); a case series of three patients with bilateral homonymous visual field defects from bilateral ischaemic strokes reports a right horizontal wedge-shaped homonymous scotoma on perimetry in a patient with a chronic left occipital stroke and acute right thalamic ischaemia, and notes that two of the three patients suffered sequential bilateral strokes and were unaware of the initial scotoma (PMID 30339636); and a lesion-to-field correlation study reports the relationship between peripheral homonymous hemianopia and lesion location using cytoarchitectonic mapping (PMID 21623227); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and this is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that the stroke PRODUCES the visual field defect, so this edge records that posterior-circulation infarction is a documented cause of a homonymous scotoma, not that a scotoma produces a stroke. No causation is established in the direction the edge name suggests, and the edge may not be presented that way. Beyond direction, the located designs do not establish that any individual scotoma is stroke-related: the primary cohort requires acute occipital stroke as an entry criterion, so it contains no stroke-free comparison group and cannot estimate the probability that a given scotoma is vascular; the case series is three patients selected precisely for the rarity of their bilateral presentation and is not a frequency estimate; and the lesion-correlation study addresses where lesions map to field defects rather than how often defects occur. A clinically important additional limit is the located report that two of three patients in the case series were unaware of the initial scotoma, so a defect may be clinically silent and its presence in a record cannot be assumed. Individual claims require a dated posterior-circulation or occipital infarction with neuroimaging, a dated perimetry or formal visual field result, and documented visual field testing rather than subjective report.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is ischaemic infarction of the occipital visual cortex or the adjacent optic radiations, supplied by the posterior cerebral artery, producing a contralateral homonymous field defect because the visual pathway has already decussated at the optic chiasm; the vector accounts for the homonymous character of the defect rather than the scotoma being a retinal or optic-nerve phenomenon, and the located case series additionally documents a wedge-shaped homonymous scotoma arising from a thalamic lesion, which places thalamocortical and corticothalamic projections in the anatomical scope of the same vascular route; the mechanism is classified as thrombotic-or-vascular to match the registry's uniform treatment of this target identity, which carries THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR on all nine of its existing incoming edges.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at posterior-circulation-cohort, case-series, and lesion-correlation class, and framed as an ETIOLOGIC edge whose direction is the reverse of the edge name, which the causation status states outright: the occipital-stroke cohort is the anchor that both establishes the ranking of stroke as the commonest cause of homonymous field defects and quantifies persistence at 36 percent beyond one year with a specific breakdown of 5 hemianopias, 5 quadrantanopias, and 3 scotomas (PMID 34487632); the case series is the anchor that supplies the discrete homonymous scotoma phenotype and the clinically important observation that a defect may be clinically silent, with the patient unaware of the initial scotoma (PMID 30339636); and the lesion-correlation study supplies the cytoarchitectonic mapping that grounds the occipital and optic-radiation anatomy in the mechanism (PMID 21623227). Because the relationship is etiologic rather than consequential, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, states the reverse direction in the causation status, and requires neuroimaging plus formal visual field testing rather than subjective report.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary cohort requires acute occipital stroke at entry, so it is a stroke-only sample with no comparator and cannot estimate how frequently any given scotoma is vascular; its 36 patients are small and its perimetry was performed at onset with follow-up beyond one year, so the 13-of-36 persistence figure is a selected survivor count rather than a population estimate; its OCT-derived ganglion cell and nerve fibre layer findings are mechanistic correlates and not clinical outcomes, and the paper's stated purpose is the elusive relationship between field defect and retinal change, not incidence; the case series is three deliberately unusual patients, one 83 years old, so it supports the existence and anatomy of the phenotype and nothing about frequency; the lesion-correlation study addresses field-defect geometry rather than aetiology; NO located anchor reports how often a homonymous scotoma presenting to an eye clinic is ultimately attributed to stroke, which is the quantity an individual claim would need; and no located anchor reports a transient ischaemic attack as a cause of a transient scotoma, which is the more common presentation and is recorded as an unresolved gap. Multiple-sclerosis and migraine are reviewed as competing rather than complementary aetiologies on this file, and are registered separately at ranks 4 and 2 so that the differential is visible on the file.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Migraine with visual aura, which the located visual-aura systematic review names among the commonest visual phenomena and which is difficult to distinguish clinically from transient ischaemic attack and from epilepsy, so the distinction between a transient vascular and a transient migrainous defect must be made on the time course
Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and other posterior-circulation processes producing similar field defects
Epileptic visual phenomena, which the located occipital-epilepsy cohort reports as simple visual hallucinations in 92 percent of cases and as misdiagnosed in 40 percent
Retinal and optic-nerve disease producing a non-homonymous defect, which a single-field confrontation test may not distinguish from a post-geniculate one

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Scotomatous visual symptoms are among the commonest reported visual aura phenomena in migraine, and the located evidence is unusually explicit about the differential this creates: a systematic review of prospective and retrospective systematic recordings of visual aura symptoms, drawing on 11 retrospective and 3 prospective studies and finding that the number of distinct visual phenomena reported per study ranged from 2 to 23, identifies the most common as flashes of bright light, foggy vision, zigzag lines, SCOTOMA, small bright dots, and heat-wave or water distortion, and states that migraine aura is associated with increased cardiovascular risk and is often clinically difficult to distinguish from other serious neurological disorders such as transient ischaemic attacks and epilepsy (PMID 31146673); a tertiary-care analysis of 165 patients classifies aura by ICHD-III and profiles visual aura type, duration, laterality, and its relation to migraine (PMID 33927518); and a systematic review addresses the differentiation of visual symptoms between retinal migraine and migraine with aura, that is between the two migraine presentations in which a scotomatous defect may appear (PMID 40873917); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that migraine PRODUCES the transient scotomatous visual symptom, so this edge records migraine as a documented cause of a transient scotoma and not that a scotoma produces migraine. Beyond direction, the located evidence is weaker than the edge's own differential warning implies: the systematic review pooled no frequencies and reports only the ranked order of reported phenomena, so scotoma is documented as commonly REPORTED without a rate, and the number of distinct phenomena varied from 2 to 23 across the included studies, which means the reported ranking depends heavily on how each study elicited and coded symptoms; the 165-patient analysis is a single tertiary centre in one country with an observational questionnaire design, which is not a population prevalence estimate; and the retinal-versus-with-aura differentiation review addresses a distinction between two migraine subtypes rather than establishing migraine as the cause of any given scotoma. The edge's most important limitation is the one the primary anchor itself raises, namely that a transient scotomatous defect is difficult to distinguish from transient ischaemic attack and from epilepsy, so an individual attribution requires the time course and associated symptoms rather than the visual phenomenon alone.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is the cortical spreading depression wave of migraine aura propagating through occipital visual cortex and producing a transient positive or negative visual phenomenon, including a scotomatous defect of variable density and duration, that resolves as the wave completes and leaves no permanent field loss; the vector is named as a spreading cortical phenomenon rather than a vascular or structural lesion because the defect in migraine aura is transient and typically resolves completely, and this is the anatomical reason the same clinical finding carries a different weight in a migrainous and a vascular aetiology, which the located systematic review states explicitly by grouping transient ischaemic attack and epilepsy among the disorders from which aura is difficult to distinguish.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review, tertiary-cohort, and systematic-review-comparative class and framed as an ETIOLOGIC edge whose direction is the reverse of the edge name, stated in the causation status: the visual-aura systematic review is the anchor that places scotoma among the commonest reported visual aura phenomena and, more importantly, the anchor that documents the differential against transient ischaemic attack and epilepsy, which is the located basis for requiring time-course-based attribution (PMID 31146673); the 165-patient ICHD-III-classified analysis supplies the contemporary single-centre profile of aura type, duration, and laterality (PMID 33927518); and the retinal-versus-with-aura differentiation review supplies the located evidence that the two migraine presentations carrying scotomatous symptoms must be distinguished from one another rather than pooled (PMID 40873917). Because the relationship is etiologic and because the primary anchor documents an active differential, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the reverse arrow, and requires the time course and associated neurological symptoms rather than the visual phenomenon alone for any individual attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary systematic review pooled NO frequencies and reports only a ranked list of reported visual phenomena, so scotoma is established as commonly REPORTED and not as occurring at any particular rate; the number of distinct phenomena reported per included study ranged from 2 to 23, so the ranking is sensitive to symptom elicitation and coding, and the review's own stated conclusion is a proposal that an official list of aura types be developed, which concedes the field is not standardised; the 165-patient analysis is a single tertiary centre in one country using an observational questionnaire design with no control group and is not a population estimate; the retinal-versus-with-aura review is a differentiation synthesis rather than an aetiology study; NO located anchor reports what proportion of patients presenting with a transient scotomatous defect are ultimately diagnosed with migraine, which is the quantity an individual claim would need; and no located anchor reports the time course that distinguishes migrainous from ischaemic scotoma in a form usable as a decision rule, although the primary anchor states the distinction is difficult. The cerebrovascular-accident and seizure-disorder edges on this same file are registered as competing aetiologies of the identical presentation, so the three edges together express a differential rather than three independent routes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Transient ischaemic attack, which the located systematic review names as a serious neurological disorder from which migraine aura is often clinically difficult to distinguish and which requires time-course and vascular-risk assessment rather than symptom shape alone
Epileptic visual phenomena, particularly occipital lobe epilepsy, which the same review names as a competing difficult-to-distinguish disorder
Retinal migraine, which the located differentiation review addresses as a distinct presentation requiring separation from aura of typical migraine
Persistent or permanent homonymous field loss, which is not the migraine-aura phenotype and points instead to a structural or vascular cause

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Occipital lobe epilepsy produces simple visual phenomena and persistent visual field defects at substantial rates, and the located cohort quantifies both while documenting how often the diagnosis is missed: a longitudinal study of 24 adult occipital lobe epilepsy patients identified over 12 months from 1548 patients in a neurologist's service and followed over 12 years reports that occipital lobe epilepsies comprise 5 to 10 percent of focal epilepsies, that 92 percent of these patients had simple visual hallucinations, that these were MISDIAGNOSED IN 40 PERCENT OF CASES, that 75 percent had co-morbid interictal migraine, that 38 percent had VISUAL FIELD DEFECTS, that only 33 percent achieved long-term remission, and that only 2 of 10 patients with a structural aetiology were seizure-free (PMID 33900448); a study of visual search disorders in patients with acute homonymous visual field defects addresses the perceptual consequences of a defect of documented vascular origin, which is the comparator class for the field component of an epileptic presentation (PMID 19500605); and the lesion-to-field cytoarchitectonic study supplies the post-geniculate anatomy that a focal occipital seizure discharges within (PMID 21623227); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that focal occipital seizure activity PRODUCES the visual phenomenon and the field defect, so this edge records occipital lobe epilepsy as a documented cause of a scotomatous or field defect and not that a scotoma produces epilepsy. The located evidence is additionally self-limiting in an important way that is registered rather than glossed: the cohort reports that the simple visual hallucinations were misdiagnosed in 40 percent of cases, which means that in a substantial fraction of real presentations the epileptic origin is not recognised, so a documented visual-field defect attributed elsewhere may in fact be epileptic, and conversely a recorded defect without a seizure diagnosis may understate the epileptic cause. The cohort is small at 24 patients drawn from a single neurologist's service, so it is enriched for complex or diagnostically uncertain cases and does not estimate community prevalence, and it reports adult disease only. Individual claims require a dated epilepsy diagnosis with electroencephalographic support, an explicit account of semiology, and a dated formal visual field result, with the reviewing clinician noting that a normal interictal electroencephalogram does not exclude occipital lobe epilepsy.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is focal epileptiform discharges in occipital visual cortex producing either brief positive phenomena during the ictal event or a persistent post-ictal or ictal visual field defect where discharge is prolonged or where a structural lesion is present, the latter being the case in the minority of patients with an identified structural aetiology in the located cohort; the mechanism is classified NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION to match the existing registry precedent for this target identity, which already carries that category on two incoming edges, though the located cohort describes a functional cortical discharge rather than a degenerative process and that mismatch is recorded here rather than resolved by inventing a category outside the controlled vocabulary.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at longitudinal-cohort, perceptual-comparison, and lesion-correlation class and framed as an ETIOLOGIC edge whose direction is the reverse of the edge name, stated in the causation status: the occipital-epilepsy cohort is the anchor that supplies both the 92 percent simple-visual-hallucination rate and the 38 percent visual-field-defect rate, and more importantly the anchor that documents the 40 percent misdiagnosis rate, which is the located justification for keeping this edge visible on a visual-field-defect file at all (PMID 33900448); the visual-search study supplies the perceptual comparator for a documented field defect and supports requiring formal testing rather than subjective report (PMID 19500605); and the lesion-to-field study supplies the post-geniculate anatomy within which a focal occipital discharge occurs (PMID 21623227). Because the relationship is etiologic and the primary anchor documents frequent diagnostic failure, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the reverse arrow, and requires electroencephalographic support and semiology rather than a defect alone.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary cohort is 24 adult patients identified from a single neurologist's outpatient service over 12 months and followed for 12 years, so it is small and referral-enriched, and it explicitly notes that little data exist on adult occipital lobe epilepsy in medical cohorts as opposed to surgical and paediatric series; its 38 percent visual-field-defect rate is in 9 of 24 patients and carries no confidence interval; its 40 percent misdiagnosis figure describes simple visual hallucinations rather than visual field defects specifically, so it must not be read as a 40 percent misdiagnosis rate for scotomas; its 5-to-10-percent and 7.7-percent focal-epilepsy proportions are drawn from the same single service; the visual-search study addresses acute homonymous defects of vascular origin and is a comparator rather than evidence about epileptic aetiology; the lesion-correlation study addresses field geometry rather than epilepsy; NO located anchor reports how often a patient presenting with a scotoma is later diagnosed with occipital lobe epilepsy, which is the quantity an individual claim would need; and the located cohort reports 75 percent co-morbid interictal migraine, which means migraine and epilepsy overlap heavily in this exact population and the two aetiologies registered on this same file are not cleanly separable. The mechanism category mismatch, a functional cortical discharge filed under NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION to follow registry precedent, is disclosed rather than hidden.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Migraine with visual aura, reported as co-morbid interictal migraine in 75 percent of the located occipital-epilepsy cohort, so migraine and epilepsy overlap heavily in this exact population and the two aetiologies on this file are not cleanly separable
Transient ischaemic attack, named by the located visual-aura systematic review as a disorder from which aura is difficult to distinguish
Structural occipital lesions such as tumour or vascular malformation, present in the minority of the located cohort with a structural aetiology and carrying a materially different prognosis
Non-epileptic functional visual phenomena and conversion, which must be excluded before an epileptic attribution

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the located cohort reports visual field defects in 38 percent of adult occipital lobe epilepsy and simple visual hallucinations misdiagnosed in 40 percent, which together mean a meaningful share of scotomas reaching an eye clinic may have an unrecognised epileptic cause. The conservative framing states the reverse arrow, records that the 40 percent misdiagnosis figure concerns hallucinations rather than field defects specifically so it is not over-read, notes the 75 percent migraine co-morbidity that makes this file's migraine edge non-separable from this one, discloses the mechanism-category mismatch to registry precedent rather than inventing a category, and requires electroencephalographic support and semiology with the explicit caution that a normal interictal electroencephalogram does not exclude the diagnosis.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple sclerosis produces visual field defects through both pre- and post-geniculate mechanisms, and the located evidence documents each: a review of visual impairment in multiple sclerosis states that visual impairment is one of the most common and disabling manifestations of the disease, that visual dysfunction related to optic neuritis and brainstem involvement is well recognised, that visual impairment associated with POST-GENICULATE visual pathways including the optic radiations and visual cortex remains comparatively under-studied and under-recognised in clinical practice, and that increasing evidence from advanced neuroimaging, optical coherence tomography, and neuropsychological testing demonstrates that lesions affecting post-geniculate white and grey matter contribute to both symptomatic and subclinical visual dysfunction, with the abnormalities listed as HOMONYMOUS VISUAL FIELD DEFECTS, visuoperceptual dysfunction, visual cognitive impairment, and higher-order ocular motor abnormalities (PMID 42729962); a retrospective population-based single-centre study of 192 patients with multiple sclerosis reports that ocular symptoms were reported by 120 patients, determines the proportion with afferent and efferent visual disturbances, assesses visual evoked potentials in detecting visual pathway abnormality, and identifies ocular findings that represented the initial clinical manifestation of the disease (PMID 41798516); and a StatPearls chapter on optic neuritis supplies the pre-geniculate route by which the demyelinating lesion produces a field defect (PMID 32496733); recorded as an ETIOLOGIC association, with the direction of causation stated explicitly and opposite to the edge name.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The direction of causation is the reverse of the edge name and is stated in the causation status rather than argued around: the located evidence establishes that demyelination PRODUCES the visual field defect, so this edge records multiple sclerosis as a documented cause of a scotoma or field defect and not that a scotoma produces multiple sclerosis. The evidence quality is additionally uneven between the two anatomical routes and that is registered rather than smoothed: the post-geniculate route is described by its own anchor as comparatively UNDER-STUDIED and UNDER-RECOGNISED in clinical practice, so the best-characterised route, optic neuritis, is represented here by a tertiary StatPearls chapter rather than by a primary cohort, and that asymmetry is disclosed. The primary cohort is single-centre and retrospective, uses structured questionnaires completed at routine visits, and reports ocular symptoms in 120 of 192 patients without a comparator population, so it establishes that ocular involvement is common in multiple sclerosis rather than estimating how often a given scotoma is demyelinating. Individual claims require a dated multiple sclerosis diagnosis meeting contemporary criteria with lesion documentation, a dated optic neuritis history or neuroimaging evidence of post-geniculate involvement, and a dated formal visual field result.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is immune-mediated demyelination at one of two points in the visual pathway, the pre-geniculate optic nerve producing a monocular defect through inflammatory optic neuritis, and the post-geniculate optic radiations or visual cortex producing a HOMONYMOUS defect through demyelinating white and grey matter lesions; the two-route description is adopted directly from the located anchor, which names both mechanisms and identifies the post-geniculate route as under-recognised, and it matters clinically because a monocular field defect and a homonymous field defect localise to different sides of the chiasm and therefore imply different underlying disease, so the reviewing clinician must characterise the defect's laterality before attributing it.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at narrative-review, population-based-retrospective-cohort, and tertiary-reference class and framed as an ETIOLOGIC edge whose direction is the reverse of the edge name, stated in the causation status: the post-geniculate review is the anchor that establishes both anatomical routes, names homonymous visual field defects as one of the manifestations of post-geniculate involvement, and documents that this route is comparatively under-studied and under-recognised in practice, which is the located basis for keeping the edge visible on a visual-field-defect file (PMID 42729962); the 192-patient single-centre cohort is the anchor that quantifies how common ocular symptoms are in a multiple sclerosis population and identifies ocular findings that were the initial clinical manifestation (PMID 41798516); and the optic neuritis reference supplies the pre-geniculate route (PMID 32496733). Because the relationship is etiologic and the two routes have unequal evidence, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the reverse arrow, discloses the tertiary-reference status of the optic neuritis anchor, and requires defect laterality to be characterised before attribution.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is a narrative review rather than a systematic review, and it explicitly characterises the post-geniculate route as under-studied and under-recognised, so its own framing concedes an evidence gap that this edge inherits rather than resolves; the 192-patient cohort is retrospective, single-centre, questionnaire-based at routine visits, with 162 of 192 patients female and 54 percent aged 20 to 30, a demographic concentration that limits generalisation, and it reports ocular symptoms as a self-reported count rather than a perimetry-derived field-defect prevalence; the optic neuritis anchor is a StatPearls tertiary reference chapter rather than a primary study or pooled analysis, which is disclosed rather than presented as equivalent evidence; NO located anchor reports what proportion of patients presenting with a scotoma are ultimately diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, which is the quantity an individual claim would need; and no located anchor reports a homonymous field-defect prevalence in any multiple sclerosis cohort, so the post-geniculate route remains characterised qualitatively rather than quantitatively in the located evidence. The registry already carries a multiple-sclerosis to optic-neuritis edge, and no chain is created by this batch because this file authors no optic-neuritis edge.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Clinically isolated syndrome or a first demyelinating event not yet meeting multiple sclerosis criteria, which must be distinguished before the multi-sublast diagnosis is applied
Retinal and optic-nerve disease producing a non-homonymous defect, including age-related macular change and glaucoma, which are more common in the same age band

Migraine with visual aura, which the located occipital-epilepsy cohort reports as co-morbid interictal migraine in 75 percent of patients and which is a frequent competing explanation for a transient defect
Toxic or metabolic optic neuropathy, including from alcohol or chemotherapeutic agents, producing a symmetric field deficit

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because visual impairment is among the most common and disabling manifestations of multiple sclerosis and because the located anchor specifically identifies homonymous field defects from post-geniculate involvement as under-recognised in clinical practice, which is a documentation gap a benefits record is likely to share. The conservative framing states the reverse arrow, discloses that the best-characterised route is represented by a tertiary reference rather than a primary cohort, reports the 192-patient cohort's demographic concentration and self-reported symptom counting, and requires the defect's laterality to be characterised because monocular and homonymous defects localise to different sides of the chiasm and imply different disease.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 82 (2026-09-27): four bounded ETIOLOGIC association edges added - scotoma to cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals (rank 1, THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR), scotoma to migraine-headaches (rank 2, NEUROENDOCRINE_CASCADE), scotoma to seizure-disorder (rank 3, NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION), and scotoma to multiple-sclerosis (rank 4, IMMUNE_MEDIATED), all classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The catalog scotoma is a visual field finding rather than a condition, so all four edges record documented CAUSES of that finding and every causation status states the reverse arrow explicitly. Anchors are the 36-patient occipital-stroke cohort reporting 26 of 36 (72 percent) with a field defect at onset and 13 of 36 (36 percent) persisting beyond one year including 3 homonymous scotomas, with GCIPL and RNFL thinning (PMID 34487632); the three-patient bilateral stroke case series reporting a wedge-shaped homonymous scotoma and that two of three patients were unaware of the initial scotoma (PMID 30339636); the cytoarchitectonic lesion-to-field study (PMID 21623227); the visual-aura systematic review identifying scotoma among the commonest reported phenomena and naming transient ischaemic attack and epilepsy as difficult-to-distinguish alternatives (PMID 31146673); the 165-patient ICHD-III tertiary analysis of aura (PMID 33927518); the retinal-versus-with-aura differentiation review (PMID 40873917); the 24-patient 12-year adult occipital-epilepsy cohort reporting 92 percent simple visual hallucinations misdiagnosed in 40 percent of cases, 75 percent co-morbid interictal migraine, and 38 percent visual field defects (PMID 33900448); the acute homonymous field-defect visual-search study (PMID 19500605); the post-geniculate multiple sclerosis review naming homonymous field defects and documenting the route as under-recognised (PMID 42729962); the 192-patient multiple sclerosis ophthalmology cohort reporting ocular symptoms in 120 patients (PMID 41798516); and the StatPearls optic neuritis chapter, disclosed as the weakest evidence class among that edge's three references (PMID 32496733). Glaucoma and cataracts are withheld as scope-mismatched against the located evidence, and the transient-ischaemic-attack route is recorded as an unresolved gap rather than authored without an anchor.
